regions.summary: Altay prefecture almost whole (Altay city, Fuyun, Habahe, Fuhai, Burqin, Qinghe, Jeminay) plus Beitun, Altai range and the Irtysh and Ulungur basins.

candidates.name: Altay
candidates.meaning: "Golden mountain" (Mongol/Turkic), the Altai range; the prefecture and seat city carry the name.
candidates.fit: The region is 99.8% of Altay prefecture, and Altay city is its seat; the range runs along the north of it. Kazakh form Altay, same spelling as the usual English.
candidates.recognisability: Current prefecture and city; the Altai range is widely known.
candidates.source_note: “阿勒泰”即“金山”之意

candidates.name: Irtysh
candidates.meaning: The Irtysh (Kazakh Ertis, Chinese Eerqisi), Siberia's great river, which rises in the Altai and crosses the region from east to west.
candidates.fit: Runs through Fuyun, Altay, Burqin, Beitun and Habahe, so through the heart of the region; the Kazakh majority form is Ertis, but Irtysh is the English name people look up.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 121 hits with 新疆, top ones about this river basin.
candidates.source_note: 额尔齐斯河从湿地南侧由东向西横穿而过 (Koksu wetland, Altay)

candidates.name: Kanas
candidates.meaning: Kanas Lake in the Altai, deep glacial lake in Burqin county (Mongol, Tuva area name).
candidates.fit: Lake sits in the far north of the region, in Burqin (7% of the people), so it stands for the mountains more than for the whole region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 770 hits with 新疆; a famous tourist lake.
candidates.source_note: 位于阿尔泰山脉中，……布尔津县……境内的著名淡水湖

regions.notes: Region includes about a third of its people across the border in East Kazakhstan (Ust-Kamenogorsk side) per facts.json parents, so Altay and Irtysh both suit.

regions.summary: Karamay oil city (three districts) with the Tarbagatay basin: Tacheng, Emin, Toli, Yumin, part of Hoboksar.

candidates.name: Karamay
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Qaramay, "black oil", after the asphalt seeps at the oilfield.
candidates.fit: Karamay districts hold 37% of the region's people, the largest block; the city is under 1M so the big-city rule does not apply. Mandarin pinyin would be Kelamayi; Karamay is the usual English form and the one I used.
candidates.recognisability: Current prefecture-level city, well known as the oil city.
candidates.source_note: 维吾尔文：Qaramay Rayoni

candidates.name: Tarbagatay
candidates.meaning: Mongol "place with marmots", the Tarbagatay range on the Kazakh border; also the name of the Qing and early Republic district (Tarbagatay Ting).
candidates.fit: The Qing Tarbagatay Ting covered today's Tacheng, Emin, Yumin and Toli, which together are most of the region outside Karamay; the range lies just north of Tacheng. I used the Kazakh/Uyghur form Tarbagatay (people in the Tacheng basin are mixed, Kazakh large); pinyin would be Taerbahatai.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 295 hits with 新疆, top ones about this place. The mountain and the old district are both known.
candidates.source_note: 塔尔巴哈台厅……治所在今新疆维吾尔自治区塔城市……辖境相当今新疆塔城、额敏、裕民、托里等市县

candidates.name: Tacheng
candidates.meaning: "Tower city" (Chinese short form of Tarbagatay; Uyghur Chöchek, Kazakh Shäweshek).
candidates.fit: Seat of the prefecture; city holds 17% of the region's people, with Emin 20%. Does not cover Karamay, so Tarbagatay fits better.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.
candidates.source_note: 维吾尔文 Chöchek Shehiri；原称塔尔巴哈台绥靖城

regions.notes: Tacheng city was first named Tarbagatay Suijing cheng (绥靖, 'pacify and calm'); that is only the old fort name and I did not propose it. Emin (额敏, from the Emin River, Yemil of the Qara Khitai capital) is 20% and was left out as a lesser fit.

regions.summary: Western Dzungaria and Bortala valley: Wusu, Kuitun, Dushanzi, Shuanghe, Bole, Jinghe, Wenquan, around Ebinur Lake.

candidates.name: Bortala
candidates.meaning: Mongol, roughly "grey-green steppe"; the Bortala river and the Mongol autonomous prefecture.
candidates.fit: Bole, Jinghe and Wenquan hold 38% of the people and the whole prefecture is inside the region. Used the usual English form Bortala (pinyin Boertala); the towns here are mostly Mandarin-speaking.
candidates.recognisability: Current prefecture; the Bortala river has its own article.
candidates.source_note: 博乐市是博尔塔拉蒙古自治州首府……博尔塔拉河

candidates.name: Wusu
candidates.meaning: Mongol usu, "water"; the Qing settlement was Kur Kara Usu, "black water".
candidates.fit: Wusu city is the single largest unit (32% of the people, 89% of its own). The Qing city built here was Qingsui (庆绥), which I did not propose.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.
candidates.source_note: 1757年……称库尔喀喇乌苏；1772年修筑庆绥城，仍名库尔喀喇乌苏

candidates.name: Ebinur
candidates.meaning: Ebinur Lake (Aibi), a salt lake in Jinghe at 189 m, the second lowest spot in Xinjiang; Mongol-origin name, meaning not confirmed in my sources.
candidates.fit: Lake lies at 83.0 E, 44.9 N, near the region's centre of mass, with the Kuitun, Jing and Bortala rivers all ending in it.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 211 hits with 新疆, top ones about this lake basin.
candidates.source_note: 艾比湖位于中国新疆博尔塔拉州精河县境内；44.883°N 83.000°E

regions.notes: Jinghe (精河, Jing river, 'crystal river' in the Qing) is not a pacify name and also fits at 16%. Dushanzi and Kuitun are small parts.

regions.summary: North slope of the Bogda range and the plain beyond: Midong (Ürümqi north), Fukang, Jimsar, Qitai, Wujiaqu, a corner of Changji.

candidates.name: Beiting
candidates.meaning: "Northern court": the Tang Beiting Protectorate (Beshbalik, Uyghur 'five cities') seated at the ruins in Jimsar.
candidates.fit: Seat (Beiting old city) is in Jimsar, inside the region; the Tang Ting prefecture had Jinman (Jimsar), Pulei and others, covering the Fukang to Qitai belt where most of the region's people live.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article for the protectorate, 462 hits with 新疆, top ones about this place.
candidates.source_note: 府治在庭州（今中国新疆吉木萨尔北庭镇北）

candidates.name: Bogda
candidates.meaning: Mongol bogd, "sacred"; the Bogda range, peak 5,445 m, with Tianchi lake on its north side in Fukang.
candidates.fit: Range stands over the whole southern edge of the region (Fukang, Midong, Jimsar, Qitai); the peak itself is at about 88.3 E, 43.8 N, just at the southern edge or over it.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki articles for the range and the peak, 241 hits with 新疆.
candidates.source_note: 海拔5,445米，位于东经88.3度，北纬43.8度

candidates.name: Qitai
candidates.meaning: Uncertain: from the seventh Qing watchtower ('seven' sounds like qi), from well-platforms, or from Khitan.
candidates.fit: Largest by area (36% of the region, 18% of the people); 'Gold Qitai' was one of Xinjiang's four old great cities.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: “奇台”地名的来源存在多种说法

candidates.name: Midong
candidates.meaning: "East of Miquan": district made in 2007 from Miquan city and Dongshan district.
candidates.fit: Largest unit at 30% of the people, but a new administrative name made from a direction word on a lost name, so it reads as part of a whole.
candidates.source_note: 2007年由原乌鲁木齐市东山区和昌吉回族自治州米泉市合并而成

regions.notes: Fukang (阜康, 'prosper and be at ease', Qing gift name) is 17% and sits at the foot of Bogda, if Anita wants a county name.

regions.summary: Changji city, Hutubi and most of Manas on the north-Tianshan plain, with part of Toutunhe and Wujiaqu fringe.

candidates.name: Changji
candidates.meaning: Chinese rendering of the Uyghur/Mongol name Sanji; its meaning is not given in the sources I read.
candidates.fit: Changji city holds 39% of the people (75% of the city); it is the seat of the prefecture. The city is under 1M, so it is not reserved. Mostly Mandarin-speaking, so pinyin.
candidates.recognisability: Current prefecture seat and county-level city.
candidates.source_note: 昌吉回族自治州的州府

candidates.name: Hutubi
candidates.meaning: From the Hutubi river (Hutukebai), Dzungar Mongol for "auspicious", or "place with a spirit".
candidates.fit: Whole county, 33% of the people; avoids repeating the city name of the prefecture.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: “呼图壁”因呼图克拜郭勒（今呼图壁河）而得名……意为“吉祥”

candidates.name: Manas
candidates.meaning: Oirat "patrol" or "guard"; the Manas river, which ends in Manas Lake.
candidates.fit: Manas county holds 20% here (and 7% of Shihezi's region); the river runs on the boundary with the Shihezi region, so it is shared.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article for the county; the epic Manas is Kyrgyz and a different place, which lowers its fit.
candidates.source_note: 得名于流经于此地的玛纳斯河，“玛纳斯”在卫拉特语中意为“巡逻者”

candidates.name: Suilai
candidates.meaning: "Pacify and bring (the people) to come": the Qing name of today's Manas county seat (1778 to 1954).
candidates.fit: Old name of Manas county only, a minority part.
candidates.source_note: 乾隆四十三年（1778）置绥来县治……1954年2月1日，改绥来县为玛纳斯县

regions.notes: Suilai rejected for its pacify meaning; Manas is the current name and works as the alternative.

regions.summary: Shihezi city (52%) and Shawan county (38%), plus a corner of Manas.

candidates.name: Shihezi
candidates.meaning: "Stone river": a small stream with a stony bed east of the town.
candidates.fit: City holds 52% of the people (99.9% of itself), seat of the Eighth Division; under 1M, so a plain city name fits.
candidates.recognisability: Current prefecture-level city.
candidates.source_note: 东有泉水汇成的小河，其底多石，因以得名

candidates.name: Shawan
candidates.meaning: "Sand bay" (Chinese name, old Shawan is a town in the county).
candidates.fit: County holds 38% of the people and 67% of the area; Shihezi city was part of Shawan until 1976.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city (2021).
candidates.source_note: 2021年1月，经国务院批准撤销沙湾县，设立县级沙湾市

regions.summary: Ghulja (Yining city, 68%) and the nearby part of Yining county (31%) in the Ili valley; very small on the map.

candidates.name: Ghulja
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Ghulja, Kazakh Qulja, Qing Turkic Gholja; the city of the Ili valley, nicknamed the flower city.
candidates.fit: City (68%) and county (31%) are both Ghulja in Uyghur, Qulja in Kazakh; Uyghur is the largest speech community here, so I used the Uyghur romanisation Ghulja. Chinese 'Yining' derives from the old Ningyuan (宁远, 'pacify the far'), which is why I put Ghulja first.
candidates.recognisability: Standard English alternative for Yining, appears on simplemaps as Ghulja.
candidates.source_note: 拉丁维吾尔文：Ghulja Shehiri；清代突厥语地名称固勒扎

candidates.name: Yining
candidates.meaning: Chinese name, from Ili plus ning ('peace'), after the Qing county Ningyuan (宁远, 'tranquil/pacify far').
candidates.fit: The current city and county; the same place as Ghulja, in Mandarin.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city and the prefecture seat.
candidates.source_note: 伊宁县原名“宁远县”，始建于清光绪十四年（1888年），因县治宁远城而得名

regions.notes: Ghulja and Yining are the same place; it is a choice of form. Another unit name, Ili, is on region 10 so it is not repeated here.

regions.summary: Ürümqi's west side: most of Xinshi district and part of Shayibake (Xishan, development zone, Diwopu airport area).

candidates.name: Shayibake
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Saybagh (probably sai 'stream bed' plus bagh 'garden'); a district name, not confirmed in sources I read.
candidates.fit: Holds 36% of the people (40% of the district); Xinshi is the bigger unit at 63%.
candidates.recognisability: Current district of Ürümqi; Uyghur form Saybagh. I used the Mandarin spelling.
candidates.source_note: 沙依巴克区（维吾尔语：سايباغ رايونى）

candidates.name: Xinshi
candidates.meaning: "New city district"; Uyghur Yengisheher, 'new city'.
candidates.fit: Largest unit at 63% of the people, but a generic modern district name.
candidates.source_note: 维吾尔文：Yëngisheher Rayoni

regions.notes: Few good options in this small city region. Diwopu (地窝堡, 'dugout', the airport name) has only 68 hits with 新疆 and no article of its own, so I left it out.

regions.summary: Ürümqi's north-east side: Shuimogou district (50%), part of Tianshan, Xinshi and Midong.

candidates.name: Shuimogou
candidates.meaning: "Watermill gully", the stream with watermills and hot springs; Uyghur name Bulaqtagh, "spring mountain".
candidates.fit: District holds 50% of the people (88% of the district).
candidates.recognisability: Current district; known for the Shuimogou hot springs and park.
candidates.source_note: 维吾尔文：Bulaqtagh Rayoni

regions.summary: Lower Ili valley west of Ghulja: Huocheng, Qapqal, Horgos, with the border and some Kazakhstan land (about a third of the people).

candidates.name: Ili
candidates.meaning: The Ili river, which flows west through the region to Lake Balkhash; also the name of the prefecture.
candidates.fit: River forms the boundary between Huocheng and Qapqal here and runs on into Kazakhstan, which fits the region's cross-border part. Ghulja region (n=7) on its east end is not named Ili.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article for the river; the prefecture and valley are widely known.
candidates.source_note: 全长1439公里。发源于天山山脉，流经中国新疆伊犁哈萨克自治州与哈萨克斯坦阿拉木图州，最终注入巴尔喀什湖

candidates.name: Almaliq
candidates.meaning: Turkic "apple place" (Almalik, Almaliq): capital of the Chagatai khans, in Huocheng northwest of Shuiding town.
candidates.fit: Ruins in Huocheng county, the largest unit (29%); the Chagatai capital sat at its centre.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 103 hits with 新疆, top ones about this city and its khans.
candidates.source_note: 阿力麻里（今新疆霍城县水定镇西北）

candidates.name: Huocheng
candidates.meaning: From the Horgos (霍尔果斯) fort town; Uyghur Qorghas, 'fortress'. The Qing county seat Suiding (绥定, 'pacify and settle') is not used.
candidates.fit: County holds 29% of the people (all of it); next is Qapqal Xibe 17%.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 霍城县，即霍尔果斯拱宸城……光绪十四年设绥定县治

regions.notes: Region includes land across the border (Almaty and Jetisu regions, 32% of people), so a river name fits better than a county name. Horgos city is a small part.

regions.summary: Old centre of Ürümqi: Shayibake (50%) and Tianshan (48%) districts, the walled city and Hongshan area.

candidates.name: Ürümqi
candidates.meaning: Probably Oirat Mongol "beautiful pasture"; some give an old Saka reading as "willow grove".
candidates.fit: The most central region, with Tianshan district (the Qing walled city) and the south-west centre; named after the city as the brief says. Mandarin and Uyghur forms are the same in English.
candidates.recognisability: The city.
candidates.source_note: 乌鲁木齐为蒙古语，意为“优美的牧场”

candidates.name: Dihua
candidates.meaning: "Enlighten and civilise": the name given to Ürümqi by the Qianlong emperor in 1763, used until 1954.
candidates.fit: Same place, but it is a civilising frontier name for a mixed Uyghur, Hui, Kazakh city.
candidates.source_note: 乾隆帝将乌鲁木齐城赐名为迪化城，“迪化”解释为“启迪教化”

regions.notes: Dihua is rejected for its meaning and because the city name is already used for this region.

regions.summary: Turpan basin and the south Ürümqi mountains: Turpan city (45%), part of Ürümqi county, Dabancheng, Toutunhe.

candidates.name: Turpan
candidates.meaning: Meaning disputed; one reading is Turkic and Hephthalite for "place of long residence".
candidates.fit: Turpan city holds 45% of the people (77% of it). Uyghur is the main speech here, so I used the Uyghur-based Turpan (pinyin Tulufan) which is also the usual English.
candidates.recognisability: Current prefecture-level city, known for the oasis and the basin.
candidates.source_note: 古称吐鲁番（Turpan），其意有争议……语义即“久居之地”

candidates.name: Gaochang
candidates.meaning: "High and prosperous": Han garrison commandery of 327, then the Gaochang kingdom (Qocho) and the Uyghur Qocho; today also the Turpan city district.
candidates.fit: Seat (Karakhoja) is east of Turpan city, inside Turpan city's area of the region; named for the whole basin in the Tang and Uyghur periods.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki articles (Gaochang commandery, Qu clan kingdom, Gaochang district), 911 hits with 新疆.
candidates.source_note: 前涼建興十五年（327年）……置高昌郡

candidates.name: Dabancheng
candidates.meaning: "Pass town" (daban, Turkic for mountain pass), the Dabancheng valley on the road to Turpan.
candidates.fit: District holds only 9% of the people but 28% of the area; known from a famous folk song.
candidates.recognisability: Current district of Ürümqi.
candidates.source_note: 2002年……达坂城镇……划归乌鲁木齐市南泉区管辖

regions.notes: Region ties Turpan city's urban east to Ürümqi's mountain county, an odd cut, but Turpan is the only large unit. Turpan Prefecture's other half (Shanshan) is in region 14.

regions.summary: Upper Ili valley: Xinyuan, Nilka, Zhaosu, Tekes, part of Gongliu and Yining county, around the Tekes, Kunes and Kash rivers.

candidates.name: Tekes
candidates.meaning: The Tekes river, the main source of the Ili (Kazakh Tekes); Turkic, probably from teke, 'wild goat'; not confirmed in my sources.
candidates.fit: River and county in the south of the region, with Zhaosu in its basin; county 13% of people but river drains Tekes and Zhaosu, the south half.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, famous for its eight-trigrams town; the river has its own article (35 hits with 新疆).
candidates.source_note: 特克斯河……是伊犁河的支流之一

candidates.name: Xinyuan
candidates.meaning: "New source": county name from the Republic (Kunes county renamed).
candidates.fit: Largest unit at 28% of the people (all of the county), home of the Narat grassland.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.

candidates.name: Kunes
candidates.meaning: The Kunes river (Uyghur Künes), rising in the Narat mountains, which waters Xinyuan and Gongliu; meaning not confirmed.
candidates.fit: Runs the length of the northern half (Xinyuan, Gongliu, Tekes junction).
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 222 hits with 新疆 but several about Hejing's Kunes town.
candidates.source_note: 巩乃斯河……發源於那拉提山，是伊犁河的支流之一

regions.notes: Zhaosu (昭苏, Uyghur Mongghulküre) and Nilka (尼勒克) are 14% each and were not proposed.

regions.summary: East Xinjiang: Hami city (56%), Shanshan (26%), Barkol, Mori and Yiwu.

candidates.name: Hami
candidates.meaning: Chinese form of Uyghur Qumul (Kumul); meaning not settled in my sources. Also the Ming Hami garrison (卫, 1406 to 1476) with its seat in today's Hami city.
candidates.fit: City holds 56% of the people (99.9% of it), and the whole of Hami prefecture's people are here. I used Hami because it is the usual English form (melons, the Ming guard); Kumul is the Uyghur form used by many locals outside the city.
candidates.recognisability: Current prefecture-level city; the Hami garrison is documented in CHGIS.
candidates.source_note: 哈密卫（卫，1406-1476）今新疆哈密市

candidates.name: Shanshan
candidates.meaning: Ancient oasis kingdom of Shanshan (Loulan) whose name the county reuses; Uyghur Pichan.
candidates.fit: County holds 26% of the people, the second largest unit.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.

candidates.name: Barkol
candidates.meaning: Turkic Barköl, probably "tiger lake" (bars plus köl); a lake and steppe at the foot of the Tianshan, Kazakh autonomous county.
candidates.fit: Holds 8% of the people but 19% of the area, the steppe to the north.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.

regions.notes: Neighbour name on the map is Dunhuang (south-east). Barkol meaning is my reading, not from a source I read.
